subject: Provisioning safeguard & monthly remedy tiers negotiation
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@everbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@everbank.com
Date: 2026-11-11T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: EverBank SLA redline and monthly remedy expectations

Markus — thanks for the call earlier. I've attached our redline (EverBank_SLA_redline_v2.pdf). Two quick asks up front so we can keep procurement moving: 

1) Baseline uptime: our procurement committee is pushing for 99.95% for prod-facing endpoints (ap-south excluded) as a requirement for go-live. If Redwood cannot meet that in the standard template, we'll need commensurate monthly remediation that effectively protects our revenue.

2) Monthly remedy cap: proposal from EverBank side is 20% of the monthly invoice as an aggregate cap (we prefer no per-incident carveouts). If you have a different model (tiered banding), please show numbers with examples against a $150k monthly spend.

Also flag: we run scheduled nightly batch models that have different latency and availability characteristics — we need a maintenance exception for batched inference windows and clarity that those don't count toward prod availability.

Can you review and get us a clear redline/response by EOD tomorrow? procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Procurement Lead — Cloud & Infrastructure
EverBank

Attachment: EverBank_SLA_redline_v2.pdf (PDF, 24 pages)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@everbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-11T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EverBank SLA redline and monthly remedy expectations

Jordan — appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Quick read-through notes and an attached counter-proposal (RK-proposed_sla_amendment.docx):

- Baseline uptime: our standard hosted offering guarantees 99.9% across multi-AZ prod endpoints. We can propose a 99.95% anchor for a Dedicated/Dedicated-Plus commit (we'd need to size dedicated pools). If you want 99.95% in the hosted template, there will be a pricing delta to cover the additional redundancy and throughput guarantees.

- Monthly remedy: we typically use a tiered credit band tied to the monthly invoice: 1) 99.9–99.5% => 5% credit; 2) 99.5–99.0% => 10% credit; 3) <99.0% => 20% credit — with an aggregate monthly cap defaulting to 15% of monthly charges. We included an example worksheet in the attachment showing how this maps to a $150k spend.

- Batched inference: agree that batched/off-peak windows should be treated differently. Proposal: exclude scheduled batch windows that are declared in the mutual action plan (MAP) and limited to a daily maintenance window (up to 4 hours). Anything outside those declared windows will be measured against prod availability.

Laura & Ben looped for legal/contract and commercial detail. If you prefer, we can run a short 30-min call tomorrow to walk the numbers with your procurement team.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0146

Attachment: RK-proposed_sla_amendment.docx (Word doc, 8 pages)

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@everbank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@everbank.com
Date: 2026-11-12T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EverBank SLA redline and monthly remedy expectations

Markus — thanks for the quick reply and the worksheet. A couple of clarifications before we bring legal in: 

- Pricing delta: we need the delta spelled out in $/month for a committed 4 GPU-pool dedicated environment sized for the baseline throughput we discussed. Can you put numbers beside the 99.95% proposal so finance can model it?

- Monthly cap: 15% feels lower than our committee's comfort zone; the 20% cap is a hard ask unless you can justify the economic tradeoff in writing (or offer a step-up for the first 6 months). Could we consider a pilot period with a 20% cap for months 1–6 and then 15% thereafter?

- Aggregation: we prefer the remedy to be applied at invoice-level (aggregate) rather than per-incident payouts; the worksheet suggests per-incident banding. Would you accept an aggregate calculation that converts total monthly availability shortfall into a single monthly credit?

Forwarding to legal after we confirm the commercial numbers.

Jordan
On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 11:03 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Jordan — appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Quick read-through notes and an attached counter-proposal...

Attachment: EverBank_SLA_redline_v2.pdf (PDF)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@everbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: EverBank SLA redline and monthly remedy expectations — legal redline

Jordan (and team) — looping in the legal redline and a few drafting points. I attached a markup (redline_markup.docx). Highlights: 

1) Monthly cap: Redwood can accept an aggregate monthly cap of 15% as the default. We can provision a pilot concession: 20% cap for months 1–6 provided EverBank commits to a 12-month Reserved Capacity agreement. That gives us a predictable commitment window to justify heavier redundancy.

2) Measurement & aggregation: we will accept invoice-level aggregation. Language: "Monthly Availability Shortfall" will be measured as the weighted-average availability across the billed services, converted to a single monthly credit applied to the subsequent invoice. We added precise timing (5 business days post-month-end for calculations, 30 days to apply the credit).

3) Maintenance exceptions: propose a narrowly-defined "Declared Batch Window" clause — customers must notify at least 5 business days in advance and include the window in the MAP. We will exclude up to 6 hours per day of declared batch processing from availability calculations if properly scheduled. For unannounced or emergency maintenance, standard carveouts apply.

4) Severity & remediation ramp: clarified what constitutes "service unavailability" vs degraded latency for routing and failover. For latency-based SLOs we propose a different remedy ladder (lower credits) since latency regressions are often operational rather than systemic.

If EverBank accepts the pilot terms, Ben and Markus: please update the commercial worksheet with the dedicated-cost delta and we'll put this into the DocuSign packet. Jordan — if you can confirm the commitment term and target dedicated sizing, we'll produce the final numbers.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: redline_markup.docx (Word doc, 6 pages)

From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@everbank.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T15:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Provisioning safeguard & monthly remedy tiers negotiation — decision for pilot

Laura/Markus/Ben — discussion at procurement & finance this afternoon went well. We can proceed on the following: 

- Pilot path accepted: 6-month pilot with a 20% monthly remedy cap for months 1–6, then 15% thereafter; in exchange EverBank will execute a 12-month Reserved Capacity commitment (we'll sign that concurrently).

- Baseline uptime: we'll accept 99.9% for hosted but will finalize the 99.95% for Dedicated when you share the $/month delta and confirmed sizing. Finance asked for the exact monthly delta by EOD Monday so they can run cost scenarios.

- Aggregation: we accept the invoice-level aggregation approach Laura proposed.

Next steps: Markus / Ben — please include the dedicated sizing & delta in the HubSpot deal (link below) and send a DocuSign packet with the pilot amendment + MAP. I'll route it for signature once legal confirms the redline.

Thanks everyone — let's aim to get the packet out Monday.

Jordan Ellis
Procurement Lead — EverBank
j.ellis@everbank.com
